action: Maersk customers and partners: watch for company updates on what data was involved, be alert to invoices or shipping messages that look unusual, and verify any payment-detail change by phone.
exec: A breach at a company Maersk acquired gave attackers a way in at a major logistics firm; Maersk says no sensitive data has been disclosed.
plain: Shipping company Maersk confirmed that an intruder took data from systems of a company it acquired. A criminal group called WhiteArmor demands $5 million and says it will publish about 100GB of data.
summary: Maersk said an intruder breached systems of a company it previously acquired and stole data. The WhiteArmor group claimed the attack and says it holds about 100GB (unverified), threatening to publish it unless paid $5 million. Maersk says no sensitive data has been disclosed.
title: Maersk confirms data theft; WhiteArmor demands $5 million

validation.note: Maersk's statement as reported by BleepingComputer; no second publisher found in the record. Attack date not disclosed.

review.note: Single publisher marked corroborated and 'legacy system' not in source; now single_source, wording matches BleepingComputer, 100GB marked unverified
